analysis.summary: Spain enter this quarter-final as the dominant side of the 2026 World Cup — nine goals scored and none conceded across five matches, with clean-sheet wins over Austria (3-0) and Portugal (1-0) in the knockouts. Belgium have been more expansive and erratic, needing extra time to edge Senegal before demolishing the USA 4-1, but now face a critical blow with Amadou Onana ruled out for the rest of the tournament after suffering a torn ACL against the USA. Spain's historical dominance over Belgium (six wins in seven all-time meetings, 13-1 aggregate in the last five 21st-century clashes) reinforces their status as clear favourites, while Belgium's best hope rests on De Bruyne's creative return and a disciplined counter-attacking game to push the match into extra time.
analysis.home_form: Spain have been the standout defensive unit of the 2026 World Cup, keeping five consecutive clean sheets: 0-0 vs Cape Verde (June 15), 4-0 vs Saudi Arabia (June 21, Yamal scored his first WC goal and Oyarzabal scored twice), 1-0 vs Uruguay (June 26), 3-0 vs Austria in the Round of 32 (July 2, Oyarzabal twice and Porro), and 1-0 vs Portugal in the Round of 16 (July 6, Merino as a second-half substitute with an injury-time header). Mikel Oyarzabal leads Spain with at least four tournament goals. Head coach Luis de la Fuente has an unchanged, fully fit squad, and the same XI is expected: Simon; Porro, Cubarsi, Laporte, Cucurella; Rodri, Pedri; Yamal, Olmo, Baena; Oyarzabal.
analysis.away_form: Belgium topped Group G but with inconsistent results: 1-1 vs Egypt (June 15), 0-0 vs Iran (June 21), and a 5-1 rout of New Zealand (June 26, Trossard MOTM). In the Round of 32 on July 1, they trailed Senegal 1-0, fought back to 1-1 through the 86th minute and won 3-2 in extra time via Tielemans' late penalty. Against the USA on July 6 they won convincingly 4-1 — De Ketelaere scored twice — but lost Onana to an ACL tear in the 19th minute. Kevin De Bruyne was rested entirely for the USA match as a squad-management decision and is expected to start here. Belgium have scored 13 goals in five games but conceded four, showing defensive vulnerability under pressure.
analysis.h2h: Spain lead the all-time head-to-head record against Belgium with six wins, one draw and no losses across seven meetings. The 21st-century record is emphatic: the last five encounters have all ended in Spanish victories, 13-1 on aggregate. The most recent clash was a 2-0 Spain win away in Brussels in September 2016. Belgium's sole competitive win over Spain was at Euro 1980 (2-1). The two nations have not previously met at a FIFA World Cup.
injuries_news: Amadou Onana (Belgium, CM) - OUT for the remainder of the World Cup with a confirmed torn ACL in his right knee, suffered in the 19th minute of the USA match on July 6. Recovery timeline is 7-8 months.
Kevin De Bruyne (Belgium, AM) - AVAILABLE; was deliberately rested for the USA match and is fully expected to start against Spain.
Spain - No injuries or suspensions reported for any player. Full squad available, and an unchanged XI from the Portugal game is anticipated.
key_factors: Spain's impenetrable defence (5 clean sheets, 0 goals conceded) is the defining tactical reality — Belgium must become the first team in this tournament to score against La Roja, against a back four of Cucurella, Cubarsi, Laporte and Porro shielded by Rodri.

Onana's ACL injury fundamentally changes Belgium's shape: without his press-triggering, the Tielemans-Vanaken double pivot sits deeper and more passively, which suits Spain's positional-play style perfectly and reduces Belgium's counter-attacking thrust.

Kevin De Bruyne's return adds elite late-game creativity and set-piece danger; if Belgium can keep the score level into extra time, his ability to unlock defences in tight spaces becomes a serious threat.
Lamine Yamal (17 dribbles completed in the tournament) and Dani Olmo provide Spain width to expose Belgium's centre-back pairing (Ngoy, Mechele), who lack top pace against dynamic wide play.

Historical H2H and psychological edge: Spain have beaten Belgium in all five 21st-century meetings 13-1 aggregate, and Belgium must overcome that record in a knockout fixture — historically this pattern heavily favours La Roja.
Venue and rest: SoFi Stadium is a neutral setting for both sides; both teams had four full days of recovery since their July 6 matches — no fatigue differential.
